name: Financial Statements & Accounting
description: Building the four statements, ratio families + DuPont, working-capital / cash conversion cycle, and 3-statement linkage. Interview-prep fundamentals.

cards.term: Accrual basis vs cash basis — when are revenue & expenses recognized?
cards.definition: Accrual: revenue when EARNED, expense when INCURRED — regardless of cash timing. Cash basis: only when cash moves. GAAP uses accrual.
Recognize expenses in the SAME period as the revenue they help generate (e.g. COGS hits when the sale happens, not when inventory was bought or paid for).

cards.term: A sale or purchase "on account" creates what?
cards.definition: Sale on account → Accounts Receivable (asset). Purchase on account → Accounts Payable (liability). No cash moves yet.

cards.term: What is COGS — and what is NOT in it?
cards.definition: Cost of goods SOLD: the cost of inventory actually sold this period. Buying inventory and paying suppliers are separate balance-sheet / cash events, NOT expenses.

cards.term: Interest expense for one year on a "5-year, $X note at r%"?
cards.definition: r × full outstanding principal X. "5-year" = maturity date, NOT "repay 1/5 of principal each year."

cards.term: Income tax expense — what's the base?
cards.definition: rate × PRE-TAX income (EBT). Accrued but unpaid → Income Tax Payable (liability).
Ending RE = Beginning RE + Net Income − Dividends.

cards.term: Where do dividends hit the statements?
cards.definition: Reduce equity (inside Retained Earnings) and show as a financing cash outflow. They are NOT an income-statement expense — they're a distribution of profit.

cards.term: Golden rule when the balance sheet won't balance?
cards.definition: Find the real error. NEVER plug Retained Earnings — RE is fixed by the roll-forward, it is not a balancing figure.

cards.term: CFO (indirect method): starting point and adjustments?
cards.definition: Start with Net Income; ADD non-cash expenses (depreciation, amortization, losses); SUBTRACT gains; then +/− changes in working capital.
Operating ASSET up → cash DOWN (subtract). Operating LIABILITY up → cash UP (add). Asset up = cash parked; liability up = cash held onto.

cards.term: Cash actually paid to suppliers, from accrual COGS?
cards.definition: Cash paid = COGS + ΔInventory − ΔAP. (Inventory build consumes cash; AP build conserves it.)

cards.term: Gain on sale of an asset — IS, CFO, and CFI treatment?
cards.definition: IS: only the GAIN is recognized. CFO: SUBTRACT the gain (cash isn't there). CFI: FULL proceeds. Rule: in CFO, gains subtract, losses add back.

cards.term: The three sections of the cash flow statement?
cards.definition: Operating (CFO), Investing (CFI), Financing (CFF). Their sum = change in cash, which ties to the BS cash line.
Current Assets / Current Liabilities.
(Current Assets − Inventory) / Current Liabilities. Strips the least-liquid current asset (sometimes prepaids too).
Due or realizable within ~1 year. A 5-year note's principal is NON-current and is excluded from current liabilities.
(Revenue − COGS) / Revenue.
Operating Income (EBIT) / Revenue.
Net Income / Revenue.
Net Income / Total Assets.
Net Income / Shareholders' Equity.
Total Liabilities / Shareholders' Equity (or interest-bearing debt / equity — state which version you mean).
EBIT / Interest Expense. How many times operating earnings cover interest.
Revenue / Total Assets. Sales generated per $ of assets.
COGS / Inventory. Times inventory cycles per year.
Revenue / Accounts Receivable.
Turnover = sales per $ of asset (activity). Return = profit per $ of asset (profitability). High turnover ≠ high return.
ROE = Net Margin × Asset Turnover × Equity Multiplier = (NI/Rev) × (Rev/Assets) × (Assets/Equity).
Total Assets / Shareholders' Equity — the leverage lever in DuPont.
Profitability (net margin), Efficiency (asset turnover), Leverage (equity multiplier). Leverage amplifies BOTH return and risk.

cards.term: Two roads to the same ROA?
cards.definition: Fat margin / slow turnover (luxury goods) vs thin margin / fast turnover (grocery). Margin × turnover can land at the same ROA.
AR / Revenue × 365 = 365 / Receivables Turnover. Days to COLLECT from customers.
Inventory / COGS × 365 = 365 / Inventory Turnover. Days to SELL inventory.
AP / COGS × 365. Days to PAY suppliers.
CCC = DIO + DSO − DPO. Tied-up legs (inventory, receivables) add; the supplier-financed leg (payables) subtracts.

cards.term: What does a NEGATIVE cash conversion cycle mean?
cards.definition: You collect from customers BEFORE paying suppliers → suppliers finance operations for free → growth self-finances and throws off cash. E.g. Amazon, Dell.

cards.term: The two "wires" linking the three statements?
cards.definition: (1) Net Income: bottom of IS → top of CFO AND into Retained Earnings on the BS. (2) Ending Cash: bottom of CFS → Cash line on the BS.
Pretax income −$10 → tax −$4 → Net Income −$6.
CFO: Net Income −$6, add back depreciation +$10 → net cash +$4. Cash rises $4.

cards.term: Depreciation +$10, 40% tax rate — balance-sheet effect & does it balance?
cards.definition: Assets: Cash +$4, PP&E −$10 → assets −$6. Equity: RE −$6 (from NI). It balances: −$6 = −$6.

cards.term: Why does depreciation INCREASE cash in isolation?
cards.definition: It's a non-cash expense that lowers taxable income → lower cash taxes. Tax shield = depreciation × tax rate = $10 × 40% = $4.

cards.term: The three tie-outs that must ALWAYS hold?
cards.definition: (1) BS balances: Assets = Liabilities + Equity. (2) CFS change in cash = BS cash beginning → ending. (3) RE rolls: beg RE + NI − dividends = end RE.
